candidates.description: The system must operate on Linux or Solaris server environments.

candidates.name: Client Access Options
candidates.description: The system must be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client.

candidates.name: Supported Web Browsers
candidates.description: When accessed through a web browser, the system must support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 or later.

candidates.name: Assistive Technology Access
candidates.description: The system must be accessible with screen-reading software, screen-magnification software, and other assistive technology programs intended to increase accessibility.

candidates.name: Relational Database Backend
candidates.description: The system must use a fully relational database back end.

candidates.name: Standards Compliant HTML
candidates.description: Web-based components must produce standards-compliant HTML output.

candidates.name: Configuration Migration
candidates.description: The system must provide separate development and training environments and support migration of configurations from those environments to production.

candidates.name: Role Based Access Control
candidates.description: The system must control user rights and privileges through security groups or roles that support access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups.

candidates.name: OPAC Feature Preservation
candidates.description: The Management Processes requirements must not constrain the functionality or features of the Online Public Access Catalog module.

candidates.name: Management Data Specifications
candidates.description: The product must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the Management Processes.

candidates.name: Process Documentation
candidates.description: The product must provide thorough high-level descriptions of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.

candidates.name: Online System Help
candidates.description: The system must provide online help in HTML that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and descriptive and illustrative of all system functions.

candidates.name: Error Feedback
candidates.description: The system must provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback and must provide low-level query-specific feedback through the front-end interface to Local and Global System Administrators.

candidates.name: Staff Authentication
candidates.description: The system should support streamlined staff terminal login using either an employee card such as an RFID badge or individual username and password credentials, with username and password available as a fallback and card-based login not required.

candidates.name: Report Template Management
candidates.description: System administrators should be able to create report templates that staff can run as-is or modify for individual needs without compromising result accuracy. Administrators should be able to restrict which filters and display fields staff may alter, such as allowing a call-number range or display-field changes while preventing changes that would expose deleted items.

candidates.name: Report Permission Administration
candidates.description: The system should provide distinct, fine-grained and easily administered permissions controlling who may create and clone reports. System administrators should be able to create shared folders that allow or prohibit staff from running specific reports or running ad hoc reports against specified data sets.

candidates.name: Multi-Record Query Designer
candidates.description: The system should provide a user-friendly query interface for bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, and financial records. Staff should be able to select query fields, choose values from picklists, choose regular expressions from a drop-down menu, and use Boolean operators, while administrators control staff access to tables and fields.

candidates.name: Executive Reporting
candidates.description: The system should provide predefined reports for library boards and other external consumers, including basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid.

candidates.name: Activity Cross Tabulation
candidates.description: Activity reports must show traffic and usage volume, including check-outs, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled, with cross-tabulation by terminal, branch, library system, hour, patron age range, patron type, and patron location.

candidates.name: Privacy Preserving Archives
candidates.description: The system must archive transactions in a form that protects patron privacy as defined by State Law while retaining useful demographic statistics.

candidates.name: Periodic Management Reports
candidates.description: The system should provide periodic reports covering bibliographic records with holds; items not checked out for a configurable number of days; item-level holds; invalid item types; in-transit items with outstanding holds; items in transit beyond a configurable number of days; last copies; long call numbers; missing items; bibliographic records without item records; and patrons with invalid home libraries.

candidates.name: Query Criteria Display
candidates.description: The system should display the query selections together with report results so users can see the criteria used to generate the report.

candidates.name: Report Queue Visibility
candidates.description: Staff should be able to see the position of their report in the queue of reports waiting to run.

candidates.name: Patron Behavior Statistics
candidates.description: The system should produce statistics for understanding and predicting patron behavior and material use, including average return speed for a particular book, likelihood of renewal, and the percentage of check-outs at a branch that are renewals.

candidates.name: Anonymized Demographic Statistics
candidates.description: The system should produce demographic statistics such as transactions by geographic region and age range, using anonymized data from which information that could identify a patron has been deleted.

candidates.name: Material Volume Reporting
candidates.description: The system must report the volume of material in a specified library at any point in time, based on new acquisitions, items on shelves, and items in circulation, with breakdowns such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books.

candidates.name: Branch Capacity Interface
candidates.description: The system should provide an interface showing the capacity of all branches.

candidates.name: Shelf Space Analysis
candidates.description: The system must compare, for each material genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, percentage of the collection, and percentage of total shelf space, with reports runnable per library and per system.

candidates.name: Uncataloged Inventory Control
candidates.description: The system must control inventory of uncataloged materials such as paperback books and children's board books, support quick distribution with minimal branch labor, identify how such material is used, and count its transactions in circulation statistics and reports.

candidates.name: Batch Item Transfers
candidates.description: The system must provide a utility for transferring batches of items between branches, including querying candidate materials, saving queries for reuse, manually selecting titles from results, changing selected item locations, moving items by changing the location field or generating pull lists, and reverting items to their original locations after a set period.

candidates.name: Missing Damaged Reports
candidates.description: The system should provide reports of missing and damaged items by branch.

candidates.name: In Transit Reporting
candidates.description: The system must generate a merged report of items in transit for more than a configurable number of days, showing results by branch and by system and combining transit-to and transit-from information for front-line staff.

candidates.name: Item Purge Management
candidates.description: The system must provide utilities and reports for identifying item records to purge using customizable criteria, including items missing for more than a configurable number of months and items with a discard or weed status. It must also support status-conversion reports, last-copy reports, effective deletion of volume and copy entries, and identification of records without attached items.

candidates.name: Deletion Tracking
candidates.description: The system must count and track deletions of records such as item and patron records by location and by system.

candidates.name: Patron Characteristic Filtering
candidates.description: Queries and reports must be limitable or groupable by patron age range, ZIP code, county of residence, home branch, patron type, and preferred language.

candidates.name: Inactive Patron Reporting
candidates.description: The system should generate a configurable report of patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during a configurable number of preceding days, with results configurable to system, home library, county, and similar organizational scopes.

candidates.name: Transaction History Retention
candidates.description: The system must maintain transaction history for a configurable number of days and retain monthly and annual aggregate information indefinitely.

candidates.name: Transaction Grouping
candidates.description: The system must group transactions by hour, terminal, branch, and system and support queries across all transaction types or a selected transaction type, including check-ins, check-outs, fines collected, and patron registrations.

candidates.name: Check In Type Counts
candidates.description: The system must count check-ins individually and cumulatively by book drop, terminal, and user or self-service check-in.

candidates.name: Check Out Type Counts
candidates.description: The system must count check-outs individually and cumulatively by staff check-out, self check-out, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.

candidates.name: Hold Placement Counts
candidates.description: The system must count hold requests and record how each hold was placed, including at a staff desk, at a public computer inside the library, or remotely.

candidates.name: Transaction Summary Reports
candidates.description: The system must generate transaction reports for holds placed, holds filled, and check-outs by patron, library, selected groups of libraries, system, and county. Results must display check-outs and placed holds per patron and subtotal holds by type, including active, frozen, and frozen-until holds.

candidates.name: Collection Value Reporting
candidates.description: The system must generate reports of item values based on item-record data for the entire collection or a portion of it, including values for items with a specified status, such as longoverdue, items in a specified collection such as children's DVDs, or the entire collection.

candidates.name: Accounting Compliance
candidates.description: All reports and data archiving must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

candidates.name: Patron Financial Records
candidates.description: The system must attach fines, charges, waivers, and ecommerce transactions to patron and item records; track waived fines and payments by library; allow financial information to be updated easily; and support queries such as patron accounts with balances above a specified dollar amount.

candidates.name: Financial Reporting
candidates.description: The system must provide financial reports showing patron account balances by patron, home library, and system; fines and charges by time period and charge type; fines waived by time period and branch; and payments by time period and payment method, including staff desk, self-check station, and OPAC.

candidates.name: Payment Audit Ledger
candidates.description: The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments identifying the charges to which payments are applied, so that payments can be reconciled.

candidates.name: Circulation Report Suite
candidates.description: The system must support circulation reports for check-in counts, checkout counts, items overdue by a specified number of days with daily, shelf-reading, and patron-contact information, circulation by circulation modifier, category, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC data, patron county, patron home library, and age demographic, renewals, non-cataloged circulation, and total circulation with checkout, renewal, and non-cataloged breakdowns.

candidates.name: Item Report Suite
candidates.description: The system must support item reports for items added, deleted, edited, or counted; items by fines-stopped reason, creation-date range, missing status, transit origin and destination, overdue or longoverdue status, total-use thresholds, last-copy deletion, claims returned, weeding data including last circulation and number of circulations, specified bibliographic content, collection age by call number or shelving location, collection price value by call number or shelving location, and items to be batch-converted from one status to another.

candidates.name: Bibliographic Report Suite
candidates.description: The system must support bibliographic reports for record counts, edited-record counts, records added by user and library, records with no attached volumes, and records missing specified MARC fields.

candidates.name: Patron Report Suite
candidates.description: The system must support patron reports for patron counts; additions by month; new patrons by demographic category; counts by age, county, home library, profile group, or survey answer; patrons by survey answer, expiration date, barred status, inactive status, note wording, or staff-account password-change date and account expiration.

candidates.name: Hold Report Suite
candidates.description: The system must support hold reports for purchase alerts, items sent to and received for holds, IntraPINES loans by system and facility, unfilled holds, annual hold totals, and stale holds remaining on hold shelves beyond the permitted pickup period.

candidates.name: In House Use Reports
candidates.description: The system must support reports for non-cataloged in-house use counts by month and cataloged in-house use counts.

candidates.name: Transit Report Suite
candidates.description: The system must support reports of items in transit to a destination library and items in transit by sending library.

candidates.name: Bills Report Suite
candidates.description: The system must support reports for bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, detailed forgive/work/goods payments received, detailed voids, and aged debt.

candidates.name: Report Interface Types
candidates.description: The reporting interface must provide canned reports that users can run immediately or recurrently, noncanned/on-demand reports with editable selection criteria and display options, and open-template reporting that allows selection of attributes associated with circulation, items, patrons, bills, and bibliographic records for filtering and display.

candidates.name: Scheduled Canned Reports
candidates.description: Canned reports must include product-delivered templates that can run using yesterday's, last week's, last month's, or last year's data; users must be able to select multiple canned reports to run at the same time and view their output in one document.

candidates.name: On Demand Report Runs
candidates.description: The system must provide on-demand reports based on preselected criteria for uses such as maintenance and collection development.

candidates.name: Report Quick Access
candidates.description: The reporting interface must provide descriptions in pop-up boxes when users hover over canned-report or template titles, allow users to select data elements, and allow scheduling as soon as possible, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.

candidates.name: Report Export Formats
candidates.description: Report output must be available in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats.

candidates.name: Report Email Delivery
candidates.description: The system must allow users to enter email addresses for report delivery and should support an address book of regularly used addresses.

candidates.name: Recurring Report Editing
candidates.description: Users must be able to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and changing their email addresses.

candidates.name: Comparative Report Output
candidates.description: The system must support report output with comparative columns such as last month's circulation, the previous month's circulation, percentage difference, the corresponding month of the previous year, and percentage difference between the previous month and the corresponding month of the previous year.

candidates.name: Canned Report Administration
candidates.description: Authorized users must be able to add canned reports according to permission level and edit canned reports for display purposes, such as adding shelving location as a displayed field.

candidates.name: Report Queue Prioritization
candidates.description: The system must allow certain report types to be prioritized so they appear ahead of resource-consuming reports in the execution queue.

candidates.name: Item Use Metrics
candidates.description: Reports must provide total item-use counts and use counts broken down by usage date ranges, such as fiscal-year or monthly counts, and must support total circulation including checkouts, renewals, and non-cataloged circulation with a breakdown by circulation type.

candidates.name: File Based Report Filtering
candidates.description: The system must allow users to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values to filter a report.

candidates.name: Notice Reporting
candidates.description: The system must support reports for pre-overdue notices, overdue notices, and holds notices sent.

candidates.name: Pivot Table Output
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide pivot-table output.

candidates.name: Report Output Validation
candidates.description: Report output must be tested and proven accurate and dependable.

candidates.name: Report Cancellation
candidates.description: Users must be able to cancel a report that is scheduled to run or is currently running.

candidates.name: Null Value Inclusion
candidates.description: Report results must include all null and blank fields regardless of the fields being filtered or displayed.

candidates.name: Real Time Reporting
candidates.description: The system must support real-time reporting.

candidates.name: Historical Reporting Warehouse
candidates.description: The system must support historical reporting through a reporting warehouse so data can be acquired for a specified date or date range.

candidates.name: Report Criteria Transparency
candidates.description: The system must clearly define selection criteria and include the selected date criteria and report name at the top or bottom of report results.

candidates.name: Survey Name Filtering
candidates.description: Users must be able to select a survey by survey name for filtering without entering its survey identifier.

candidates.name: Deleted Last Copy Reporting
candidates.description: The system must provide reports identifying deleted items that were the last copy owned by a library system or facility, to support WorldCat updates.

candidates.name: MARC Row Consolidation
candidates.description: The system must be able to retrieve MARC record fields and display them on a single row of report data.

candidates.name: Workstation Transaction Reporting
candidates.description: The system must support reports for transactions occurring on a specified date and time, at a specified workstation, or performed by a specified staff member.

candidates.name: Generate Item Value Reports
candidates.description: The system must generate reports showing the value of items, using the purchase price or other value data in item records, for the entire collection or a selected portion. The report must support selections such as all items with status "longoverdue", all DVDs in the children's collection, and the entire collection.

candidates.name: Compliant Financial Reporting
candidates.description: The system's financial reports must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.

candidates.name: Enforce Data Retention
candidates.description: The system must archive financial data in accordance with state and local requirements and enforce retention policies, including retaining applicable audit data for seven years.

candidates.name: Associate Financial Records
candidates.description: The system must associate fines, charges, waived fines, payments, and ecommerce transactions with the relevant patron and item records, and support joining patron and item financial data when querying financial information.

candidates.name: Find High-Balance Accounts
candidates.description: Staff must be able to query patron accounts with balances greater than a user-specified dollar amount so that accounts requiring attention can be identified.

candidates.name: Update Payment Information
candidates.description: The system must allow financial information to be updated easily and must reflect a patron payment made at a front desk immediately.

candidates.name: Report Patron Balances
candidates.description: The system must provide financial reports showing patron account balances by individual patron, home library, and the library system.

candidates.name: Report Accrued Charges
candidates.description: The system must provide reports of fines and charges accrued for selectable time periods, including the last 12 months, year to date, and the last month, and by charge type such as overdue fines, damaged-item charges, and lost-item charges.

candidates.name: Report Waived Fines
candidates.description: The system must provide reports of fines waived by selectable time period and by branch or library, so waived-fine activity can be tracked against each library's budget.

candidates.name: Report Collected Payments
candidates.description: The system must provide reports of payments made for selectable time periods, payment methods, and collecting libraries or branches. Payment methods must include channels such as the staff desk, self-check station, and OPAC, and types such as cash, credit card, and check.

candidates.name: Maintain Payment Audit Ledger
candidates.description: The system must maintain a ledger of patron payments that identifies the specific charge or charges to which each payment was applied, allowing finance staff to trace every payment and reconcile accounts.

candidates.name: Design Queries Across Records
candidates.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query-design interface that works across all record types and lets staff select query fields, choose values from picklists, select regular expressions from a dropdown, and apply Boolean operators.

candidates.name: Control Query Tool Access
candidates.description: The system must let administrators control which users can access the query-design tool.

candidates.name: Create Shared Report Templates
candidates.description: The system must let administrators create report templates that are available to staff, so users requesting the same report run it with consistent criteria.

candidates.name: Run And Modify Templates
candidates.description: The system must let staff run report templates as-is or modify them within administrator-defined controls, including limits on which filters and display fields may be changed; permitted changes must not compromise the template's intended results, such as allowing a weeding report to change its call-number range or display fields without allowing it to display deleted items.

candidates.name: Clone Existing Reports
candidates.description: The system must let authorized users clone an existing report template to create a new report variant distinct from the original template.

candidates.name: Manage Report Permissions
candidates.description: The system must provide distinct, fine-grained permission levels that control who can create and clone reports and which staff can run specific reports or ad hoc reports against specified sets of data; administrators must be able to administer these permissions through shared folders that allow or disallow the relevant access.

candidates.name: Apply Role-Based Permissions
candidates.description: The system must update a user's report permissions automatically when the user's role changes, such as changing the user from Staff to Manager.

candidates.name: Provide Board Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide predefined reports for library boards covering basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and activity statistics for traffic and volume of use, including checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled; the activity data must support cross-tabulation by terminal, branch, system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location.

candidates.name: Archive Private Transactions
candidates.description: The system must retain transaction data for the period required by State law, including the unspecified period represented as X years, while protecting patron privacy by not retaining personally identifiable information and preserving data sufficient to produce useful demographic statistics.
candidates.source_priority_note: D12 identifies State-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements

candidates.name: Show Query Selections
candidates.description: The system must display the query selections or criteria together with the query results.

candidates.name: Show Report Queue Position
candidates.description: The system must show staff whether a submitted report is in the queue, how many reports are ahead of it, when it was submitted, and its status as waiting, running, completed, or failed.

candidates.name: Prioritize Reports In Queue
candidates.description: The system must allow authorized report prioritization so that important reports, such as a director's board report, can move ahead of lower-priority reports such as a staff member's ad hoc query.
candidates.source_priority_note: D12 describes report prioritization as crucial

candidates.name: Support Streamlined Staff Login
candidates.description: The system must support an optional streamlined staff login method, such as swiping an employee ID badge, while also supporting traditional individual username-and-password login as a fallback for staff without ID cards or branches without card-reader infrastructure.

candidates.name: Authenticate Individual Staff Members
candidates.description: Regardless of the login method used, the system must individually authenticate the staff member and record which staff member is logged in so that staff activity can be associated with the correct person for audit purposes; a card swipe must not bypass individual authentication.

candidates.name: Control Access By Staff Roles
candidates.description: The system must determine staff permissions from assigned security groups or roles and provide access control for individual staff members, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups. Roles must support different permission levels, including front-desk staff with access to basic reports and limited filters, department heads who can create and modify templates, and system administrators with full access to reports and permissions.

candidates.name: Administer Roles And Permissions
candidates.description: Administrators must be able to create and manage security groups or roles and assign them to staff members. Changing a staff member's permissions must be achievable by changing the person's role assignment rather than modifying individual permissions.

candidates.name: Circulation By Modifier
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a circulation-count report grouped by circulation modifier, including the modifier associated with each circulation transaction.

candidates.name: Circulation By Dewey
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a circulation-count report grouped by Dewey classification.

candidates.name: Circulation By MARC Fields
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a circulation-count report grouped or filtered by specified MARC fields.

candidates.name: Circulation By County
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide circulation counts by circulation location with a breakdown by patron county.

candidates.name: Circulation By Age
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide circulation counts by patron age demographic.

candidates.name: Items Edited Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report counting items edited during a specified reporting period.

candidates.name: Fines Stopped Reasons
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a list of items grouped or filtered by the reason that fines were stopped.

candidates.name: Overdue Items Contacts
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report of items overdue by a specified number of days and include the associated patron contact information.

candidates.name: Items By Use Count
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a list of items having a specified total use count.

candidates.name: Last Copy Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an enhanced last-copy report identifying items that are the last copy of their bibliographic work or collection grouping.

candidates.name: Items By Creation Date
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a list of items created within a specified date range.

candidates.name: Claims Returned Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report of items recorded as claims returned.

candidates.name: Weeding Circulation Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a weeding report that includes each item's date of last circulation.

candidates.name: Collection Age By Call Number
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide the age of the collection broken down by call number.

candidates.name: Collection Value By Call Number
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide the price value of the collection broken down by call number.

candidates.name: Bibliographic Edits Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report counting bibliographic records edited during a specified reporting period.

candidates.name: Bibliographic Additions Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report counting bibliographic records added by user and by library.

candidates.name: Missing MARC Fields
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report identifying bibliographic records missing specified MARC fields.

candidates.name: Patron Count By Age
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide patron counts by age demographic.

candidates.name: Patron Count By County
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide patron counts by county.

candidates.name: Patron Geographic Counts
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide patron counts broken down by county, city, and ZIP code.

candidates.name: Voter Survey Responses
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report of voter survey responses.

candidates.name: Inactive Patrons Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a list of patrons whose status is inactive.

candidates.name: Staff Password Change Dates
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report of staff accounts including the date of each account's last password change.

candidates.name: Holds Purchase Alert
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a holds purchase alert report identifying hold activity that indicates a potential purchasing need.

candidates.name: Unfilled Holds Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report of unfilled hold requests.

candidates.name: Stale Holds Report
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a report of stale hold requests.

candidates.name: Detailed Aged Debt
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an enhanced aged-debt report with detailed debt information for patrons and the applicable aging periods.

candidates.name: Report Queue Visibility
candidates.description: The reporting system must show staff the queue position and current status of their submitted reports.

candidates.name: Report Prioritization
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow authorized users or processes to prioritize selected types of reports for execution.

candidates.name: Cancel Running Reports
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow a user to cancel a report that is currently running.

candidates.name: Pivot Table Output
candidates.description: The reporting system must produce report results in pivot-table format.

candidates.name: Real-Time Reporting
candidates.description: The reporting system must support reports that use current data in real time rather than only processing a static or delayed reporting dataset.

candidates.name: Historical Reporting Warehouse
candidates.description: The system must provide a historical reporting warehouse that preserves data needed for reporting on past states and time periods.

candidates.name: Report Scheduling Options
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow a report to be run ASAP or scheduled hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.

candidates.name: Report Email Delivery
candidates.description: The reporting system must deliver report results by email in addition to making them available through the web interface.

candidates.name: Report Delivery Address Book
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an address book for selecting recipients for report delivery.

candidates.name: Text File Filtering
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow users to upload text files containing values such as barcodes or TCNs and use those values as report-filtering criteria.

candidates.name: Selection Criteria Results
candidates.description: The reporting system must display the selection criteria used to generate a report within the report results.

candidates.name: Canned Display Options
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow users to edit the display options of canned reports.

candidates.name: Report Quick Access
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a quick-access interface for reports with pop-up descriptions.

candidates.name: Report Title Tooltips
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide hover tooltips describing report titles.

candidates.name: Reporting Database Replica
candidates.description: The system must provide a separate reporting database or replica so reporting workloads are separated from the production database.

candidates.name: Background Report Processing
candidates.description: The reporting system must process long-running reports in the background without requiring the user interface to remain occupied by the report execution.

candidates.name: Report Template Management
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide management of report templates, including storing and maintaining reusable report definitions.

candidates.name: Fine-Grained Report Permissions
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide fine-grained report permissions that control who can create reports, run reports, access reports, use specific filters, and access shared report resources.

candidates.name: Reporting Environment Separation
candidates.description: The product must provide separate development and training environments for reporting functionality.

candidates.name: Environment Configuration Migration
candidates.description: The reporting system must support migration of reporting configuration between environments.

candidates.name: Accessible Report Interface
candidates.description: The report interface must provide accessibility support sufficient for staff using the reporting system, including compliance with applicable accessibility requirements.

candidates.name: Integrated Report Help
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide an online help system integrated with the report interface.

candidates.name: Three Reporting Interfaces
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide separate canned-report, on-demand-report, and open-template-reporting interfaces.

candidates.name: Snapshot Bills Reporting
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a snapshot bills report that can report bill information as it existed at a point in the past.

candidates.name: Separate Last Edit Date
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide a last-edit date that does not represent or incorporate the date of the item's last circulation.

candidates.name: Last Circulation Date
candidates.description: The reporting system must expose the date of an item's last circulation as a separate reportable field.

candidates.name: Checkin Date Excluding Renewals
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide check-in date and time separately from renewal timestamps, so reports can identify check-ins without treating renewals as check-ins.

candidates.name: Preserve Null And Blank Fields
candidates.description: The reporting system must include null and blank fields in report results rather than filtering them out.

candidates.name: Multiple Report Formats
candidates.description: The reporting system must provide report output in multiple formats, including CSV, HTML, and an Excel-compatible format.

candidates.name: Track Uncataloged Materials
candidates.description: The system must track uncataloged paperback books, children's board books, and other material as inventory before individual catalog records are available, while supporting rapid distribution with minimal branch labor and enabling staff to identify how the material is being used.

candidates.name: Count Uncataloged Transactions
candidates.description: The system must count transactions involving uncataloged material and include those transactions in circulation statistics and reports.

candidates.name: Query Transfer Candidates
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must allow staff to query for candidate materials, such as all items in the children's section that have not circulated in six months, for transfer between branches or to mobile and outreach collections.

candidates.name: Save Transfer Queries
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must allow staff to save candidate-material queries for repeated use, including monthly reuse.

candidates.name: Select Transfer Items
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must allow staff to manually select individual titles from query results when a targeted transfer is required.

candidates.name: Change Item Locations
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must allow staff to change the records of selected items so that the items move to a new location.

candidates.name: Revert Item Locations
candidates.description: The item transfer utility must provide a mechanism to return transferred items to their original location after a defined period, such as when a mobile library returns to its base.

candidates.name: Report Missing Damaged Items
candidates.description: The system must provide a report showing all missing and damaged items for each branch so collection management staff can monitor collection health and identify patterns of loss or damage.

candidates.name: Report Overdue Transit Items
candidates.description: The system must provide one report combining transit-to and transit-from items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable number of days, with results available per branch and for the entire system.

candidates.name: Identify Purge Candidates
candidates.description: The system must provide a weeding report that identifies items for purging using customizable criteria, including items that have been in status "missing" longer than a specified number of months and items with status "discard/weed."

candidates.name: Batch Change Item Status
candidates.description: The system must provide a report or operation that assists staff in converting selected items from one status to another in batch, including changing 100 items from "missing" to "discard/weed."

candidates.name: Report Last System Copies
candidates.description: The system must provide a report identifying the last copies held by a library system so catalogers can check and edit corresponding WorldCat entries before deleting or otherwise altering a rare or final copy.
candidates.source_priority_note: D15 marks the last copy report as critical

candidates.name: Delete Orphaned Records
candidates.description: The system must provide a quick, effective method for deleting volume entries together with their copy entries and for deleting records that have no items attached, to support cleanup of orphaned catalog records.

candidates.name: Track Record Deletions
candidates.description: The system must count and track record deletions by location and by library system, including the reason for each deletion, to support auditing and troubleshooting.

candidates.name: Report Shelf Space Allocation
candidates.description: The system must provide a shelf space report that compares, for each genre and format, the percentage of total circulations, the percentage of the collection, and the percentage of total shelf space, so collection managers can allocate resources.

candidates.name: Report Material Volumes
candidates.description: The system must provide a material volume report covering acquisitions, items on shelf, and items in circulation, broken down by categories such as total items, holds, adult fiction, and board books.

candidates.name: Provide Data Quality Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide data quality reports identifying items with invalid item types, items with excessively long call numbers, and bibliographic records with no item records, so staff can maintain catalog data integrity.

candidates.name: Display Item Edit Dates
candidates.description: Reports must show the date an item was last edited, where the date changes only when the item is edited and does not treat the last circulation as an edit; the edit date must not be combined with the last circulation date.

candidates.name: Linux Solaris Compatibility
candidates.description: The reporting system must operate on both Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware, including the primary and disaster-recovery/reporting server environments.

candidates.name: Open-Hours Report Processing
candidates.description: The system must process searches and reports during library open hours without disrupting circulation or other system functions, including avoiding database contention from complex reports; background queuing or read-only reporting replicas may be used to achieve this.

candidates.name: Legacy Browser Support
candidates.description: The system must support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 and later and Firefox 2.0 and later so that libraries using the existing browser installations can run the reporting system.

candidates.name: Section 508 Accessibility
candidates.description: The system must comply with Section 508 and support staff using screen readers such as JAWS and NVDA, screen magnification software such as ZoomText, and other assistive technologies. Its HTML output must use alt tags, ARIA labels, semantic structure, and standards-compliant HTML.
candidates.source_priority_note: D16 describes Section 508 compliance as non-negotiable and a legal requirement

candidates.name: Relational Database Integration
candidates.description: The reporting system must work with PINES's fully relational PostgreSQL database structure, support complex joins, and use the main relational database rather than requiring a denormalized reporting schema that can create synchronization issues.

candidates.name: Role-Based Access Control
candidates.description: The system must control permissions through security groups and/or roles for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups. It must support the Patron, Staff, Local Admin, and Global Admin access levels, with Local Admins able to run reports and configure local settings and Global Admins having full system access.
candidates.source_priority_note: D16's interview notes describe role-based access control as essential

candidates.name: Simple Role Administration
candidates.description: Administrators must be able to change a user's permissions by changing the user's role assignment, with roles being easy to administer.

candidates.name: Separate Development Environment
candidates.description: The product must provide a development environment where developers can test new reports without affecting the production environment.

candidates.name: Separate Training Environment
candidates.description: The product must provide a training environment where new staff can practice running reports without affecting production or making operational mistakes.

candidates.name: Configuration Migration
candidates.description: The system must provide export and import functionality to migrate report templates, permission settings, and other configuration from development or training environments into production.

candidates.name: OPAC Isolation
candidates.description: The management reporting system must remain separate from the OPAC so that reporting activity, including large queries, does not constrain or slow the OPAC and patrons retain fast, responsive catalog access.
candidates.source_priority_note: D16's interview notes describe separation of reporting from the OPAC as critical

candidates.name: Searchable Hierarchical Help
candidates.description: The system must provide online HTML help for staff that is hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable, and easy to navigate, including guidance on how to run reports.

candidates.name: Collection Use Analysis
candidates.description: The reports interface must enable library managers, administrators, and staff to analyze library collections and how patrons use them for planning, evaluation, and oversight.

candidates.name: Branch Capacity Analysis
candidates.description: The reports interface must enable authorized library managers and administrators to analyze branch capacity and determine the optimal distribution of the library collection across branches.

candidates.name: Patron Demographics Analysis
candidates.description: The reports interface must enable authorized library managers and staff to analyze patron demographics and interests to support planning and evaluation of library services.

candidates.name: Staff Workflow Analysis
candidates.description: The reports interface must enable authorized managers and supervisors to analyze staff productivity and workflow for oversight and service planning.

candidates.name: Financial Transaction Verification
candidates.description: The system must provide reports or analysis capabilities that allow authorized library staff and managers to track and verify financial transactions.

candidates.name: Library Report Templates
candidates.description: The product must provide report templates needed by all PINES member libraries for their management reporting activities.

candidates.name: Management Reporting Scope
candidates.description: The reports functionality must support management processes used by library managers, administrators, and staff for planning, evaluation, and oversight, rather than day-to-day patron-facing functions handled through the OPAC and circulation client.

candidates.name: Consortium Statistical Reporting
candidates.description: The system must enable the Global System Administrator, representing the PINES central IT team, to generate statistical reports for the PINES consortium as a whole.

candidates.name: Consortium-Scale Operations
candidates.description: The management processes must support a library consortium with 286 locations, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing and processing of more than 900,000 items per year.

candidates.name: Background Report Processing
candidates.description: The system must process searches and reports in the background or through a queue so that report generation during open or peak hours does not slow down circulation-client operations or other system functions.

candidates.name: Linux Solaris Server Support
candidates.description: The management processes must operate on either a Linux or Solaris server.

candidates.name: Browser Client Access
candidates.description: The management processes must be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client. Browser-based access must support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 or later.

candidates.name: Assistive Technology Access
candidates.description: The management processes must be accessible using screen-reading, screen-magnification, and other accessibility software, including JAWS, NVDA, and ZoomText, and must satisfy Section 508 requirements.
candidates.source_priority_note: D18 describes this as a legal requirement and says Section 508 compliance is mandatory

candidates.name: Inventory Capacity Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide inventory and capacity reports for library staff who use them to monitor collections and operational capacity.

candidates.name: Financial Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide financial reports for library directors and other users who need director-level financial information.

candidates.name: Cross-Branch Comparisons
candidates.description: The system must provide reports that compare relevant library data across branches so library management can evaluate branches against one another.

candidates.name: Report Queue Visibility
candidates.description: The system must allow users to view the status and contents of the report-processing queue so they can monitor reports awaiting or undergoing processing.

candidates.name: Executive Report Definitions
candidates.description: The system must provide predefined reports for boards and executive users, supporting recurring executive-level reporting needs.

candidates.name: Data Quality Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide data quality reports that help library staff identify and assess problems in the system's data.

candidates.name: Card Swipe Login
candidates.description: The system must support staff login using a card swipe so staff can authenticate without relying solely on manually entered credentials.

candidates.name: In-Transit Item Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide reports on items in transit so library staff can coordinate delivery between locations.
candidates.source_priority_note: D18 describes in-transit item reports as critical for delivery coordination

candidates.name: Missing Damaged Item Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide reports of missing and damaged items, with results available per branch so branch staff can manage local item problems.

candidates.name: Weeding Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide weeding reports that help library staff identify materials for collection-weeding activities.

candidates.name: Shelf Space Utilization
candidates.description: The system must provide reports showing shelf-space utilization so library staff can assess and plan physical collection capacity.

candidates.name: Demographic Analysis Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide demographic analysis for library staff planning programs and services.

candidates.name: Relational Database Backend
candidates.description: The management processes must use a fully relational database backend and operate correctly with the relational data structure used by the reporting layer.

candidates.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
candidates.description: The system must produce valid, standards-compliant HTML for report displays, the help system, and web-based user-interface components.

candidates.name: Configuration Migration Environments
candidates.description: The product must provide separate development and training environments and support migrating configurations, including report templates, between those environments and production through export and import.

candidates.name: Role-Based Access Control
candidates.description: The system must control user rights and privileges through security groups or roles, with access control applicable to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups.

candidates.name: OPAC Functionality Preservation
candidates.description: Changes and functionality in the management processes must not constrain or adversely affect the functionality or features of the Online Public Access Catalog.

candidates.name: Record Data Specifications
candidates.description: The product must provide complete data specifications for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by the management processes, enabling staff to understand the data structures used for queries.

candidates.name: Process Overview Documentation
candidates.description: The product must provide thorough high-level documentation of major processes, including bibliographic-record import and export, validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.

candidates.name: Online Cross-Linked Help
candidates.description: The system must provide online HTML help that is hierarchical and cross-linked, describes and illustrates all system functions, and is available without requiring staff to leave the system.

candidates.name: Actionable Error Feedback
candidates.description: The system must provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback and must provide low-level, query-specific feedback through the front-end interface to Local and Global System Administrators when report or query operations fail.

candidates.name: Vendor Data Interfaces
candidates.description: The management processes must interface with external vendor websites through published APIs and/or automated transfers of standard-format data files, including formats such as USMARC21 and EDIFACT.

candidates.name: Acquisitions Cataloging Integration
candidates.description: The management processes must use the data structures and functionality of the enterprise library automation system's Acquisitions and Cataloging modules when reporting on acquisitions and cataloging data.

candidates.name: OPAC Data Querying
candidates.description: The management processes must interact with the Online Public Access Catalog and query patron-related data created there, including holds and circulation data.

candidates.name: Relational Database Backend
candidates.description: The Management Processes reporting system must use a fully relational database back end and operate with the relational data structure without requiring denormalized reporting data.

candidates.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
candidates.description: The system must produce HTML output that validates against W3C standards for the web-based interface, online help system, and report output, supporting compatibility with different browsers and assistive technologies.

candidates.name: Environment Configuration Migration
candidates.description: The system must support migration of configurations between separate development, training, and production environments by exporting and importing templates, permission settings, and saved queries.

candidates.name: Safe Training Environment
candidates.description: The training environment must allow staff to experiment without risking production data.

candidates.name: Role-Based Access Control
candidates.description: The system must provide security groups and/or roles for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups, with permission changes managed through role assignments. It must support Global Admin full system access; Local Admin branch-level reporting and configuration; Library Manager execution of approved reports and limited template modification; Staff execution of reports within assigned permissions; and indirect Patron access through OPAC displays.

candidates.name: OPAC Performance Isolation
candidates.description: The management reporting system must remain separate from the public catalog so that running a report does not slow down the OPAC.

candidates.name: Record Data Specifications
candidates.description: The developer must provide complete data specifications and data dictionaries for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other records maintained or accessed by Management Processes, including field names, data types, and relationships so staff can write effective queries.

candidates.name: Process Documentation
candidates.description: The developer must provide thorough high-level descriptions of major processes, including bibliographic record import and export, validation of bibliographic records against internal and external authority sources, and standard reports.

candidates.name: Accessible Online Help
candidates.description: The system must provide an online help system in HTML that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and accessible to screen readers.

candidates.name: Detailed Error Reporting
candidates.description: The system must provide thorough high-level error reporting and feedback, and low-level query-specific feedback for administrators, including the relevant table, field, and type of error when a report fails.

candidates.name: Centralized Multi-Location Service
candidates.description: Management Processes must be consolidated at a central location that accepts input from and provides services to multiple library locations, providing a single source of truth for reporting data.

candidates.name: Library Automation Data Dependency
candidates.description: Management Processes must use the data structures and functionality of the enterprise-level Library Automation System, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules, while reading their data rather than managing acquisitions or cataloging.

candidates.name: Vendor Data Integration
candidates.description: Management Processes must interface with vendor websites through published APIs and/or automated transfers of standard-format data files, including formats such as USMARC21 and EDIFACT, while functioning when such vendor data is not present at every library.

candidates.name: Read-Only OPAC Integration
candidates.description: Management Processes must query patron-interface data from the OPAC, including data related to holds and circulation transactions, without modifying that data.

candidates.name: Multiple Report Output Formats
candidates.description: The reporting system must produce reports in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats, supporting web display, business-user pivot tables, and reliable data export.

candidates.name: Real-Time Historical Reporting
candidates.description: The reporting system must support real-time reports for current conditions, such as what is overdue today, and historical reports that retrieve values as they existed at a specified past date, such as a bill amount on June 30th.

candidates.name: Report Cancellation
candidates.description: The system must allow users to cancel scheduled or currently running reports, including cancellation during report processing.

candidates.name: Include Null Values
candidates.description: Reports must include null values and blank fields in their results.

candidates.name: Survey Name Filtering
candidates.description: The reporting system must allow filtering by survey name and resolve the survey name to the corresponding survey ID internally.

candidates.name: Retain Transaction History
candidates.description: The system must retain detailed transaction history for a configurable number of days and preserve monthly and annual aggregate data indefinitely.

candidates.name: Group Transactions By Dimensions
candidates.description: The system must group transaction reports by hour, terminal, branch, and system so staff can analyze activity and identify busy periods.

candidates.name: Count Check-In Methods
candidates.description: The system must count check-ins both individually and cumulatively by method, including book drop, terminal, staff/user processing, and self-service.

candidates.name: Count Checkout Types
candidates.description: The system must count check-outs both individually and cumulatively by type, including staff checkout, self checkout, staff renewal, self checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.

candidates.name: Classify Hold Placement
candidates.description: The system must report holds according to their placement method, including staff desk, public computer, and remote placement.

candidates.name: Aggregate Transaction Totals
candidates.description: The system must report holds placed, holds filled, and check-outs per patron, per library, per group of libraries, per system, and per county.

candidates.name: Provide Demographic Statistics
candidates.description: The system must provide transaction statistics by geographical region, age range, and useful demographic attributes such as ZIP code, while anonymizing the data so that personally identifiable information is not disclosed.

candidates.name: Analyze Patron Behavior
candidates.description: The system must produce statistics that help staff understand and predict patron behavior and material use, including return speed, renewal rates, the percentage of check-outs that are renewals, and the likelihood that a book will be renewed.

candidates.name: Create Report Templates
candidates.description: Administrators must be able to create report templates that can be run as-is or modified before execution.

candidates.name: Control Report Permissions
candidates.description: The system must provide fine-grained permissions that limit who can create, clone, and run particular reports.

candidates.name: Manage Shared Report Folders
candidates.description: The system must provide shared folders that can allow or prevent staff from running specific reports.

candidates.name: Show Report Queue Position
candidates.description: The system must show a user where the user's report is in the processing queue and whether it is still processing.

candidates.name: Save Reusable Queries
candidates.description: The system must allow staff to save queries and reuse them for repeated reporting activities.

candidates.name: Export Multiple Formats
candidates.description: The system must allow reports to be exported in Excel, CSV, and HTML formats, with Excel exports avoiding unnecessary duplicate rows.

candidates.name: Deliver Reports By Email
candidates.description: The system must support delivering completed reports by email.

candidates.name: Schedule Recurring Reports
candidates.description: The system must allow users to schedule reports to run on a recurring basis.

candidates.name: Query Candidate Materials
candidates.description: The system must allow staff to query for materials that are candidates for administrative actions.

candidates.name: Select Query Results Manually
candidates.description: The system must allow staff to manually select individual records from query results for subsequent administrative actions.

candidates.name: Move Items By Location
candidates.description: The system must allow authorized staff to change item records so that items are moved to a new location.

candidates.name: Revert Item Locations
candidates.description: The system must allow authorized staff to revert items to their original locations.

candidates.name: Track Record Deletions
candidates.description: The system must count and track record deletions.

candidates.name: Report Historical Data
candidates.description: The system must provide historical reporting that shows what data looked like on a specified past date, including historical shelving locations even when those locations have since changed.

candidates.name: Provide Snapshot Bills Reports
candidates.description: The system must provide a snapshot bills report that can retrieve bills information from past points in time.

candidates.name: Generate Pivot Outputs
candidates.description: The system must provide pivot-table output for reports.

candidates.name: Support Real-Time Reporting
candidates.description: The system must provide real-time reporting for activity during busy periods.

candidates.name: Cancel Running Reports
candidates.description: The system must allow users to cancel scheduled reports and reports that are currently running.

candidates.name: Include Empty Report Fields
candidates.description: The system must include null and blank fields in report results rather than excluding those records or values.

candidates.name: Expose Specific MARC Fields
candidates.description: The system must allow reports to retrieve specific MARC fields even when the fields are stored across multiple rows.

candidates.name: Show Last Circulation Date
candidates.description: The system must include the last circulation date as a field in item reports.

candidates.name: Exclude Renewals From Check-In Dates
candidates.description: The system must ensure that check-in date and time reporting does not include renewal transactions.

requirements.name: Collection And Material Use Reports
requirements.description: The reports interface must enable authorized managers, administrators, and staff to analyze collections and material use for planning, evaluation, and oversight.
requirements.priority_justification: Seven source documents call for collection and material-use analysis, and managers depend on it to plan, evaluate, and oversee collections.

requirements.name: Consortium Scale
requirements.description: The system must support a library consortium with 286 branches, 17 million annual circulations, and purchasing and processing exceeding 900,000 items per year.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-1 High Priority, and consortium-scale support is necessary for the system to serve its stated 286-branch environment.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-1 High Priority

requirements.name: Cross-Branch Performance Reports
requirements.description: The reports interface must enable analysis of performance across branches.
requirements.priority_justification: Cross-branch performance analysis is repeatedly requested across seven documents and supports oversight of the consortium as a whole.

requirements.name: Role-Based Transfer Access
requirements.description: Administrators must control rights through security groups and roles assigned to individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups, with changes to role assignments changing permissions. The library automation system must support Global Admin, Local Admin, Library Manager, Staff, and indirect Patron access through the OPAC, with report and transfer permissions appropriate to each role and transfers restricted to authorized roles, including managers, administrators, and transfer coordinators.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-4 High Priority, and D16 identifies role-based access control as essential; without it, staff cannot be reliably limited to authorized reporting and transfer actions.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-4 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe role-based access control as essential

requirements.name: Collection Analysis Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide reports on weeding data, collection age, collection value, and last-copy status. Collection-value reports must use purchase-price or other item-record data and cover the entire collection or selected portions, including status- or collection-based selections such as longoverdue items or children's DVDs. Last-copy reports must identify items that are the only copy within a selected branch, library system, consortium, bibliographic work, or collection grouping, including deleted last copies where applicable, so catalogers can update WorldCat and avoid inappropriate deletion.
requirements.priority_justification: D06 and D15 explicitly mark last-copy reporting critical, and these reports help catalogers avoid inappropriate deletion while supporting collection decisions.
requirements.source_priority_note: D06 marks last-copy reporting critical; D15 marks the last-copy report as critical

requirements.name: Item Status and Activity Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide reports on items that are missing, overdue, in transit, claimed returned, selected by use count, or associated with a fines-stopped reason.
requirements.priority_justification: Missing-item reporting is required by the fixed requirements, and the broader status reports also help staff manage overdue and in-transit materials.

requirements.name: Missing Damaged Reports
requirements.description: The system must report missing and damaged items by branch, including condition notes such as water damage or vandalism and selectable periods such as the preceding 30 days or last quarter.
requirements.priority_justification: D05 calls the per-branch report crucial for accountability, and four additional sources request missing or damaged item reporting.
requirements.source_priority_note: D05 calls the per-branch missing/damaged report crucial for accountability

requirements.name: Transit Report Suite
requirements.description: The system must provide reports for items in transit to a destination branch and items in transit by sending branch, including one report combining transit-to and transit-from items that have remained in transit longer than a configurable threshold, defaulting to seven days where specified, using a null arrival date and an overdue departure date; results must be available by branch and library system and sortable by due date.
requirements.priority_justification: D18 describes in-transit item reports as critical for delivery coordination, and delayed or untracked transfers can disrupt service across branches.
requirements.source_priority_note: D18 describes in-transit item reports as critical for delivery coordination

requirements.name: Checkout and Renewal Reports
requirements.description: The system must provide checkout and renewal reports that count transactions individually and cumulatively by staff checkout, self-checkout, staff renewal, self-checkout renewal, online renewal, and OPAC renewal.
requirements.priority_justification: Checkout and renewal counts directly support the fixed requirement for item-use reporting and help managers understand how materials are used.

requirements.name: Patron Report Filtering
requirements.description: The system must filter and group patron queries and reports by age range derived from birth date, ZIP code, county, home branch, patron type, and preferred language, and must combine filters with AND and OR logic and applicable circulation conditions.
requirements.priority_justification: D08 calls these reports essential, and demographic and circulation filtering is a central way staff answer patron-service and planning questions.
requirements.source_priority_note: D08 calls these reports essential

requirements.name: Background Report Processing
requirements.description: Long-running reports, including inactive patron reports in environments with approximately 3.5 million patrons, must execute as background operations or through a queue without occupying the user interface, and the system must cache slow activity-query results for reuse.
requirements.priority_justification: The fixed open-hours performance requirement calls for reports not to disrupt other services, and background processing helps meet that need for large, slow queries.

requirements.name: Accounting Data Retention
requirements.description: The system must archive financial data according to state and local requirements and enforce applicable retention policies, including seven years of audit data where required.
requirements.priority_justification: Applicable financial retention rules, including required audit-data periods, must be enforced to support accountable records management.

requirements.name: Assistive Technology Access
requirements.description: The system must satisfy Section 508 accessibility requirements and support screen readers including JAWS and NVDA, screen magnification including ZoomText, and other assistive technologies; web output must include appropriate alt tags, ARIA labels, semantic structure, and standards-compliant HTML.
requirements.priority_justification: D16 and D18 identify Section 508 accessibility as a legal requirement and mandatory, making assistive-technology access a compliance obligation.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-5 High Priority; D16 describes Section 508 compliance as non-negotiable and a legal requirement; D18 describes this as a legal requirement and says Section 508 compliance is mandatory

requirements.name: Branch Management Reports and Templates
requirements.description: The system must provide predefined reports and report templates needed to cover the management reporting needs of all consortium member branches.
requirements.priority_justification: Multiple source documents request management reports for consortium branches, and without suitable reports and templates branch managers would lack a consistent way to meet routine oversight needs.

requirements.name: Client And Browser Access
requirements.description: The system must be accessible through a web browser or Windows-compatible client and support Microsoft Internet Explorer 6.0 or later and Mozilla Firefox 2.0 or later.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks OE-3 High Priority and D18 calls browser/client access critical, so staff access to the system depends on this capability.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks OE-3 High Priority; D10 marks OE-4 Medium Priority; D18 marks this capability critical

requirements.name: Cross-Record Query Designer
requirements.description: The system must provide a user-friendly query designer across bibliographic, item, patron, transaction, financial, and other record types, with selectable fields, picklists, regular-expression choices, and Boolean operators.
requirements.priority_justification: A cross-record query designer lets staff build reports across the system's principal data areas, and without it many requested analyses would require custom work.

requirements.name: Data Archiving Compliance
requirements.description: Data archiving must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 and D11 require compliant financial-data archiving for auditing, so noncompliant archiving would fail the stated records obligations.

requirements.name: Financial Report Compliance
requirements.description: Financial reports must comply with standard accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 and D11 require financial reports to meet accounting practices and government auditing requirements, so reports that fail those standards would not meet the stated obligation.

requirements.name: Integrated Accessible System Help
requirements.description: The system must provide hierarchical, cross-linked, searchable HTML help that describes and illustrates system functions, is accessible within the system and to screen readers, and includes integrated online help for the reporting interface.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-3 High Priority, and accessible, searchable help lets staff learn and use reporting functions without relying solely on direct support.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks UD-3 High Priority

requirements.name: Management Reporting Scope
requirements.description: The reporting functionality must support management planning, evaluation, and oversight rather than day-to-day patron-facing functions handled by the OPAC and circulation client.
requirements.priority_justification: Five sources define management planning, evaluation, and oversight as the reporting system's scope, distinguishing it from patron-facing operations.

requirements.name: OPAC Preservation
requirements.description: Management and reporting functionality must not constrain, slow, or adversely affect OPAC functionality or patron access.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks CO-5 High Priority, and management reporting that degrades patron access would compromise the underlying library service.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks CO-5 High Priority; D16's interview notes describe separation of reporting from the OPAC as critical

requirements.name: Open-Hours Performance
requirements.description: Searches and reports must run during open or peak hours without disrupting circulation, other system functions, or the OPAC; background queues, read-only replicas, or equivalent isolation must avoid excessive database contention.
requirements.priority_justification: Five sources request safe operation during open or peak hours, and contention that disrupts circulation or OPAC access would impair the system's core use.

requirements.name: Patron Information Removal
requirements.description: The system must remove personally identifying information about patrons from retained transaction data.
requirements.priority_justification: D12 identifies patron-privacy protection as a compliance requirement, so retained transaction data must have personally identifying information removed.
requirements.source_priority_note: D12 identifies State-law retention and patron-privacy protection as compliance requirements

requirements.name: Payment Audit Ledger
requirements.description: The system must maintain a payment ledger identifying the charge or charges to which each patron payment was applied so payments can be traced and reconciled.
requirements.priority_justification: D11 marks the payment ledger CRITICAL, and tracing applied payments is needed to reconcile patron financial records.
requirements.source_priority_note: D11 marks this requirement CRITICAL

requirements.name: Record Data Specifications
requirements.description: The product must provide complete data specifications and dictionaries for authority, bibliographic, order, item, hold/request, and other accessed records, including field names, data types, and relationships.
requirements.priority_justification: D10 marks UD-1 High Priority, and accurate data specifications support the cross-record reporting the product must deliver.
requirements.source_priority_note: D10 marks UD-1 High Priority

requirements.name: Relational Database Support
